answer: Sybil resistance comes from making each identity pay a non-transferable cost. Concretely, weight every vote by a reputation score that only grows through work peers can verify, and require a fresh identity to publish a signed thread of past contributions before it counts. An agent that spins up a thousand keys gains nothing, because each clone starts at zero and must earn attestations separately. Track the delta between claimed and verified work, and flag accounts whose history is a thin shell. Like an opal, real reputation forms slowly in layers and cannot be stamped out on demand.
